note: Architectural invariants enforced by scripts/check-arch.sh. Every rule must carry what/why/fix so a failure is a repair instruction, not a verdict. Promote a review finding here when the category of mistake repeats -- see the promotion rule in AGENTS.md.

rules.what: Bare print() call in backend application code.
rules.why: print() bypasses the structured logger, so the line has no run id, no trace id and no level: it is invisible to observability and unusable in a replay. Every service logs structured events with structlog (AGENTS.md §0).
rules.fix: Replace print(...) with logger.info("event_name", key=value) using the module's existing `logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)`.

rules.what: The synchronous `requests` library is imported in async application code.
rules.why: requests blocks the event loop. One slow upstream call freezes every concurrent request on that worker, which reads as a global outage rather than a slow provider.
rules.fix: Use `httpx.AsyncClient` (or the existing ai_client / tool gateway), and await the call.

rules.why: It blocks the event loop for the whole duration, so a 2s backoff becomes a 2s stall for every other request in flight (same failure mode as the sync-requests rule).
rules.fix: Use `await asyncio.sleep(...)`, or the retry/backoff helper in the relevant client.

rules.why: A bare except also swallows KeyboardInterrupt and asyncio.CancelledError, so a client disconnect or a shutdown is converted into 'handled' and the task keeps running against a closed stream.
rules.fix: Catch `Exception as exc` (narrower if you know the type) and log it; use `except asyncio.CancelledError: raise` where cancellation must propagate.

rules.what: A service imports the HTTP layer.
rules.why: Dependencies flow one way: router -> service -> domain/infrastructure. A service importing a router inverts that, makes the service untestable without the API, and is the start of the circular import that breaks app startup.
rules.fix: Move the shared logic into the service (or a domain module) and have the router call it. See docs/harness/architecture.md §3.

rules.what: Browser-side code embeds the backend origin (:8000).
rules.why: The browser must never reach FastAPI directly: the BFF route handlers under frontend/src/app/api/** are the only client of the backend. A direct call skips the session cookie handling, the SSE translation and the error normalisation there, and breaks the moment the backend is not on localhost.
rules.fix: Call a same-origin BFF route (e.g. /api/chat) instead. `frontend/src/lib/proxy.ts` is excluded because it runs server-side.
